newsitem.title: UK: UK gives MMC more time on Freemans deal.
newsitem.headline: UK gives MMC more time on Freemans deal.

text.p: The British government said on Wednesday it had agreed to extend the deadline for the Monopolies and Mergers Commission's investigation into Littlewoods' plans to buy Freemans mail order from Sears Plc until September 22.
The MMC, which monitors competition in Britain, had been due to report to the Department of Trade and Industry on the proposed merger by July 21.

The DTI said in a statement competition and consumer affairs minister Nigel Griffiths had agreed to the extension following representations from the MMC on the complexity of the issues raised by the merger.
"In order for the MMC to be able to analyse the evidence fully and to draw sound conclusions, the reporting period should be extended to 22 September 1997," it said.

In April retailer Sears announced plans to sell its Freemans home shopping business to Littlewoods for 367.5 million pounds ($616.1 million). The deal was referred to the MMC on grounds that it would give football pools to retailing company Littlewoods around 25 percent of the UK mail order market.
The sale of Freemans is part of a sweeping reorganisation of Sears' retail empire, including the demerger of department store Selfridges and rationalisation of loss-making British Shoe Corporation.
Sears has promised to hand proceeds from the Freemans sale back to shareholders, if it gets a green light from the MMC.
Sears' shares were 3.5 pence lower at 61.5 pence by 1025 GMT.
